RagShortTexts: Concentrating cavalry needs usable ground and support; narrow routes separate front and rear.
An opening still needs flank security and a return route; stamina and messages limit repetition.

Variants.Content: Concentrated riders can pressure a chosen point if leaders, regrouping places and flank duties are clear. Woods, ditches and soft ground narrow a force and delay followers. Courage relies on horse stamina, footing and support. Without a return route, an initial advance can strand experienced men beyond their companions.

A following rider watches turns and leaves room to check his horse when those ahead halt. After contact, finding a regrouping position is safer than isolated pursuit. Attendants bring back broken lances, injured mounts and reports, all requiring attention before another departure.
